t: Other than in emergency situations, none of the funds in this Act may be used to operate telephone answering machines during core business hours unless such answering machines include an option that enables callers to reach promptly an individual on-duty with the agency being contacted.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that letting callers reach a live agency employee is a form of public access to government, so it counts as participation. But this is only an appropriations restriction on how agencies run their phone systems. It sets up no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue tied to any federal decision. General customer-service accessibility is not outside-party involvement in a government decision.
fable.s: none of the funds in this Act may be used to operate telephone answering machines during core business hours unless such answering machines include an option that enables callers to reach promptly an individual on-duty with the agency being contacted

qwen_block.w: This section imposes a procedural requirement on how federal agencies must handle incoming calls (specifically, regarding answering machines). It does not involve consultation, coordination, or decision-making input from parties outside the federal government. The 'callers' are recipients of a service, not participants in a government decision-making process.
qwen_block.s: Other than in emergency situations, none of the funds in this Act may be used to operate telephone answering machines during core business hours unless such answering machines include an option that enables callers to reach promptly an individual on-duty with the agency being contacted.

opus.w: This is a funding limit on how agencies run their phone systems. It makes sure members of the public can reach a person when they call. The tempting reading is that this counts as participation because outsiders get to talk to agency staff. That reading fails because the provision doesn't require any consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue before the government makes a decision. Callers simply get access to staff, not a role in any federal decision.
opus.s: none of the funds in this Act may be used to operate telephone answering machines during core business hours unless such answering machines include an option that enables callers to reach promptly an individual on-duty with the agency being contacted.

qwen_chat.w: This section imposes a procedural requirement on how federal agencies must handle telephone calls during business hours to ensure accessibility. It does not involve consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties regarding federal decisions, policies, or regulations. The interaction described is a standard customer service protocol, not a participatory process as defined by the inclusion of outside entities in decision-making.
qwen_chat.s: Other than in emergency situations, none of the funds in this Act may be used to operate telephone answering machines during core business hours unless such answering machines include an option that enables callers to reach promptly an individual on-duty with the agency being contacted.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that requiring callers to reach an individual implies a form of public interaction or participation in government operations. However, this is merely a procedural requirement for customer service accessibility, not a mechanism for the public to consult with, advise, or influence federal decision-making. The definition of participation requires consultation or coordination with outside parties *before* a decision is made, or involvement in advisory bodies, hearings, etc. This section simply mandates how telephone systems must be configured during business hours.
